'''Louisiana Intrastate Gas (LIG) Pipeline ''' is a natural gas pipeline in Louisiana.<ref name=source1>[http://bit.ly/2sGFvfM Louisiana Intrastate Gas (LIG) Pipeline ,] A Barrel Full, accessed September 2017</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs from Cotton Valley, Louisiana, to New Orleans, Louisiana.

==Background==
LIG, which is one of the largest intrastate pipelines in the state of Louisiana, consists of approximately 2000 miles of gas gathering and transmission systems located in 29 parishes extending from northwest and north-central Louisiana through the center of the state to south and southeast Louisiana. Current on-system market of approximately 580,000 mmbtu/d includes power plants, municipal gas systems, and industrial markets located principally in the industrial corridor between New Orleans and Baton Rouge. Processing plants owned by LIG give the system the capability to handle rich and lean gas supplies connected to the system. Connections to several interconnected pipelines and the Jefferson Island Storage facility provide access to additional system supply. <ref name = source2> [http://enlk.enlink.com/investor/investor-news/investor-news-details/2004/Crosstex-Completes-Acquisition-of-Louisiana-Intrastate-Gas-Company/default.aspx "CROSSTEX COMPLETES ACQUISITION OF LOUISIANA INTRASTATE GAS COMPANY"] EnLink accessed January 2018 </ref>

A 1985 article reported that Tenneco Inc. purchased LIG among other natural gas holdings from Goodyear Tire and Rubber Co for about $500 million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1985/06/19/business/tenneco-to-buy-gas-pipelines.html|title=Tenneco to buy gas pipelines|last=|first=|date=19 June, 1985|website=The New York Times|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=25 August, 2023}}</ref> In June 1989, it was reported that an investor resold LIG to Arkla Inc. for $170 million, which they had bought from Tenneco Inc. three months ago.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1989/06/06/Louisiana-Intrastate-Gas-resold-for-170-million/8025613108800/|title=Louisiana Intrastate Gas resold for $170 million|last=|first=|date=06 June, 1989|website=UPI|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=25 August, 2023}}</ref> Equitable Resources acquired LIG from Arkla, Inc. for $190 million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ingaa.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/30081.pdf|title=Profile of Intrastate Gas Pipelines|last=|first=|date=10 August, 1993|website=INGAA Foundation|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=25 August, 2023}}</ref> On December 02, 1998, American Electric Power (AEP)acquired LIG from Equitable Resources. In February 2004, AEP announced the sale of Louisiana Intrastate Gas Pipeline Co and its subsidiaries to EnLink Midstream Partners LP, formerly Crosstex Energy LP for $76.2 million.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ogj.com/general-interest/article/17292515/crosstex-energy-buys-lig-pipeline-co-for-762-million|title=Crosstex Energy buys LIG Pipeline Co. for $76.2 million|last=|first=|date=09 April, 2004|website=Oil & Gas Journal|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=25 August, 2023}}</ref><ref name=":0" />
